channel.title: Religion News Service - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Religion News Service (religionnews.com)

item.title: Milan church concert strikes a chord for inclusion ahead of Winter Paralympics
item.description: The choir’s concert in Milan formed part of the archdiocese’s strategy to seize the Olympic and Paralympic moment to impart Christian values.

item.title: Pope Leo will visit 4 African countries as part of his packed 2026 travel plan
item.description: The announcement sets the stage for one of the busiest papal travel schedules in years, since Leo will also be undertaking a grand tour of Italy starting in May that will take him up and down the peninsula in a half-dozen one-day visits.

item.title: Catholic bishops: Trump’s assault on birthright citizenship affronts Catholic teaching
item.description: 'By recognizing children as members of a particular political community, birthright citizenship acknowledges the intrinsic value of every human person,' the brief reads.

item.title: Attorney general announces indictment against 30 more people who protested at a Minnesota church
item.description: Protesters descended on Cities Church in St. Paul, Minnesota, on Jan. 18 after learning that one of the church’s pastors also serves as an Immigration and Customs Enforcement official.

item.title: Hegseth proclaims ‘Christ is king,’ turning Christian hope into a political slogan
item.description: and should not — point to any earthly nation or project.

item.title: Purim is raucous and chaotic. But the lesson for us may be in Esther’s strategic protest.
item.description: Esther’s greatness lies not only in her willingness to speak truth to power, but in choosing the strategic moment to do so.

item.title: Joseph Smith portrait at Morehouse sparks debate over slavery, polygamy and Black history
item.description: On Feb. 1, the Smith portrait was unveiled at the chapel named for the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. at a vespers service attended by descendants of the Smith family.

item.title: Singing protests gain momentum as non-violent but emotionally stirring rebukes to ICE
item.description: 'We're going to sing and sing and try to touch the hearts of the ICE agents,' said the Rev. Jacqueline Lewis, senior pastor at Middle Church in New York.

item.title: Black church leaders use new books to share history and hope
item.description: Released during or close to Black History Month, the books provide a faith-oriented look at African American history and analyses of women in ministry and changing demographics and technology.

item.title: A Texas student turns abandoned school into mosque in 45 days
item.description: A med student's viral renovation project became a Ramadan miracle in Lubbock, Texas — and a test of whether Muslim Americans belong.
